 Order

Accused in Special Case No.876/2022 pending before the Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC - III, Bangalore Rural District, Bangalore City, arising out of Crime No.165/2022 registered by the Kadugodi Police Station, Bangalore City, for offences punishable under Section 363, 376(3) of IPC and Sections 4, 6 and 12 of POCSO Act, is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking regular bail.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

On the basis of the complaint of 2nd respondent, who is the mother of the victim girl, FIR in Crime No.165/2022 was registered by Kadugodi Police, Bangaloru City, on 31.08.2022 against unknown persons for offence under Section 363 of IPC.
During the course of investigation of the case, on 08.09.2022 the victim girl was traced along with the petitioner in his native place.
The police thereafter, brought the victim girl and the petitioner to the police station and the petitioner was produced before the Trial Court and remanded him to judicial custody.
The victim girl was produced before the Doctor for the purpose of medical examination and her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was also recorded before the jurisdictional Magistrate.

sentences.text: Therefore, petitioner is before this Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has reiterated the grounds urged in the petition and submits that, the petitioner and the victim girl were in love.
The victim girl has not made any serious allegation against the petitioner in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
The victim girl has not co-operated for the purpose of medical examination.

Petitioner is aged about 19 years,
and he is in custody from 08.09.2022.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, the learned HCGP appearing for the 1st respondent has opposed the bail application and prays to dismiss the petition.
6. From a perusal of the material available on record, it is seen that the petitioner and the victim girl are acquainted with each other and they were in love.
The 2nd respondent, who is the mother of the victim girl had approached the police on 31.08.2022, after her minor daughter was found missing from the house from 30.08.2022 onwards.
In the complaint the 2nd NC: 2023:KHC:40833 respondent has expressed that she suspected the hand of a boy and she also had given the mobile numbers of the suspect.
The charge sheet material would go to show that the petitioner and the victim girl were traced together in the house of the petitioner in his native place.
The victim girl has not co-operated for the purpose of medical examination.

During the course of her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. by the jurisdictional Magistrate the victim girl has not made any serious allegation against the petitioner, and on the other hand, she stated that she was acquainted with the petitioner and she was in love with him.
She also has stated that she had gone along with the petitioner and they had stayed in his house in their native place along with the mother of the petitioner.
The charge sheet allegations made against the petitioner are required to be proved in a full fledged trial.

Petitioner, who is aged 19 years, without any no criminal antecedents,
is in custody from 08.09.2022 onwards.
Learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent has submitted that the victim girl has already been examined before the Trial Court and she has been treated as hostile witness in the case.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that, petitioner has made out a prima facie case for grant of regular bail.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
